title: Sell Mineral Rights in Marshall County, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Marshall County, WV
metaDescription: Marshall County minerals sit in Marcellus/Utica core acreage near Moundsville — dense horizontal units, spacing questions, and multi-generation heir splits.
heroLead: Marshall County is core Marcellus and Utica ground, and the same density that makes it attractive to operators makes the title work behind each royalty check genuinely complicated.
intro: Few counties in the state have seen as much horizontal drilling density as Marshall. Multi-well pads cluster along the Ohio River corridor and back into the hills around Moundsville and McMechen, with operators unitizing large blocks of acreage that frequently cross old farm-line boundaries drawn a century before anyone knew what a lateral was.

That density is good for production, but it complicates title in a specific way: many Marshall County tracts have been leased, released, re-leased, and partially assigned multiple times since the first vertical gas wells went in during the mid-1900s. Sorting out which lease actually governs a given royalty interest today takes a real read of the courthouse record, not only the most recent division order.

sections.heading: Why Marshall County reads as core Marcellus/Utica acreage
paragraphs: Marshall sits in the thickest part of the Marcellus fairway in West Virginia, with the Utica/Point Pleasant stacked beneath it at drillable depth in the northwestern part of the county. That stacked-pay geology is why operators here often permit multiple laterals from a single pad targeting both formations, and why spacing units in Marshall tend to run larger and denser than in flank counties further south or east.

For a mineral owner, stacked-pay development means your acreage can eventually sit under two separate royalty streams from two different formations, governed by two different unit orders — which is exactly the kind of interest that benefits from a proper title review before any sale or lease decision.

sections.heading: Spacing units and pooled acreage around Moundsville
paragraphs: Horizontal units around Moundsville and out toward McMechen commonly pool several original farm tracts into a single unit, sometimes 1,000+ acres, to accommodate long laterals. If your family's original tract predates the unit, your royalty is a pro-rata share calculated against your surface acreage's proportion of the total unit — a number that should be confirmed against the actual unit plat filed with the operator, not assumed from the tract's historical acreage alone.

Because Marshall County has multiple operators active in overlapping areas, it's also worth checking whether your interest is subject to more than one lease of record — a common leftover from older leases that were never formally released even after a newer lease was signed by a subsequent owner.

sections.heading: Multi-generation heir splits from farm-era severances
paragraphs: Marshall County's rural tracts were largely severed — mineral estate split from surface — in the early 1900s, well before most current owners were born. Four and five generations later, a single original 1/1 mineral interest is commonly split among fifteen or more descendants, many living outside West Virginia and unaware their name is on a deed book entry from 1911.

When we buy in Marshall County, we're usually working from an heir's copy of a division order or an old deed reference rather than a clean modern title. A courthouse records pull at the Marshall County Courthouse in Moundsville — deed books, will books, and any prior division orders — establishes exactly what percentage you actually hold before any number gets discussed.

sections.heading: Processing infrastructure and why it matters for lease negotiation
paragraphs: Marshall County hosts significant midstream processing capacity tied to its production volumes, which is part of why operators have been consistently willing to commit capital here even as commodity prices cycle up and down elsewhere. For a mineral owner, that infrastructure investment is a signal of long-term operator commitment to the county, but it doesn't change the fact that royalty is still calculated off wellhead or point-of-sale volumes and prices as defined in your specific lease — worth reading closely rather than assuming favorable county-wide conditions translate automatically into a favorable individual check.

Some older Marshall County leases include deduction language allowing the operator to subtract post-production costs — gathering, compression, processing, transportation — before calculating your royalty. Comparing what your lease actually allows against what's being deducted on your check is a common source of underpayment claims, and it's worth a second look if your net royalty seems low relative to reported production.

faqs.question: What does stacked-pay development mean for my royalty check?
faqs.answer: If your acreage is developed for both the Marcellus and the deeper Utica/Point Pleasant, you may eventually see two separate royalty streams from two different unit orders on the same tract, each calculated on its own pro-rata share.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my actual percentage in a large pooled unit near Moundsville?
faqs.answer: Request or locate the unit plat and pooling order filed with your operator, then compare your original tract's surface acreage against the total unit acreage. A courthouse title check confirms the tract's chain and any prior assignments that affect your net share.

faqs.question: I found an old lease from the 1970s and a newer one from a different owner — which one controls?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the earlier lease was released of record and who held the interest at each signing. This is exactly the kind of layered title question that needs a courthouse deed-book review before you rely on either lease.

faqs.question: My interest in Marshall County is split among a dozen cousins — can I sell just my share?
faqs.answer: Yes. Undivided fractional interests are sellable on their own; you don't need the other heirs to participate, and your closing only affects your percentage of the mineral estate.
